original_question: Suppose Omega is a bounded convex domain in R^2 and u solves the constant-mean-curvature Dirichlet problem div(Du/sqrt(1+|Du|^2)) = 2H in Omega with u = 0 on partial Omega. Determine how the convex level curves of u are distributed as a function of H, and if possible extend Wang's example to the case where Omega is unbounded.
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 4.2 (3*): the open problem about controlling, for zero-boundary CMC Dirichlet solutions on bounded convex planar domains, how the convex level curves are distributed in terms of H, and about extending Wang's counterexample to the nonbounded convex-domain setting.
correct_elements: Your draft very closely matches the paper's actual target. It has the right setting (a bounded convex domain Omega in R^2), the right PDE and zero boundary data, the right object of study (convexity of level curves of the CMC graph solution), and the right second task (trying to extend Wang's counterexample to the nonbounded case).
missing_details: The exact target is Section 4, Problem 4.2, not the neighboring Problem 4.3; Problem 4.2 concerns convexity of level curves, whereas Problem 4.3 asks for conditions ensuring convexity of the whole graph in the sense of positive Gauss curvature.
The notation should be tied explicitly to equation (4.1): H is a real constant, Omega is a domain in R^2, and the boundary datum is phi = 0 on partial Omega.
To make the question stand alone, 'Wang's example' should be identified internally as the cited counterexample of a CMC graph over a convex domain whose level curves are not all convex.
The paper asks to 'give a control' of the distribution of convex level curves in terms of H; it does not ask for a complete classification of all level curves or of all convex solutions.

For the nonbounded extension, the nearby context matters: the paper notes that for a nonbounded convex domain and phi = 0, solvability of the Dirichlet problem is known precisely when Omega is contained in a strip of width 1/|H|.
It is also helpful to retain the paper's planar-boundary context: phi = 0 means the graph has planar boundary.
refined_question: Let Omega be a bounded convex domain in R^2, let H be a real constant, and let u solve the zero-boundary constant-mean-curvature Dirichlet problem div(Du/sqrt(1+|Du|^2)) = 2H in Omega, u = 0 on partial Omega. Give a control, in terms of H, of how the convex members of the level-set family {u = t} are distributed. Moreover, can one extend Wang's counterexample—namely, a constant-mean-curvature graph over a convex domain whose level curves are not all convex—to the case of a nonbounded convex domain Omega (necessarily in the solvable regime, e.g. Omega contained in a strip of width 1/|H|)?
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Section 4, Problem 4.2, because it reproduces the exact Dirichlet equation (4.1) with zero boundary data on a bounded convex planar domain and asks the same two things the paper asks there: control of convex level curves in terms of H, and extension of Wang's example to the nonbounded case. The only needed sharpening is to make the reference to Wang's example self-contained and to keep the scope narrow: this is a level-curve question, not the broader neighboring question about convexity of the entire graph.
